name: popover
description: A panel of any content that opens beside the button that names it, flipping to stay on the screen and closing on Escape or a click outside, with no script.

attributes.name: data-placement
attributes.description: Which side of its button the panel opens on. start and end follow the writing direction. Where there is no room on that side it flips to the other.

attributes.name: data-max
attributes.description: The widest the panel may grow, from the width scale; it is always narrower than the viewport by a gutter each side.

children.description: The contents: ordinary flow content, such as a heading, a sentence, a form or a button.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-xs
tokens.description: The default maximum, when data-max is absent.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The least margin kept between the panel and each side of the viewport, and the space between its children.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-xs
tokens.description: The gap between the button and the panel.

tokens.name: --yeti-heading-space-after
tokens.description: The space after a heading inside the panel.

tokens.name: --yeti-duration-fast
tokens.description: How long the panel takes to fade in.

keyboard.action: On the button, opens or closes the panel.
From the button, moves into the panel; from the panel's last control, moves to what follows the button.
Closes the panel and returns focus to its button.

a11y.notes: The button needs a name, and the browser sets its expanded state from popovertarget. In Chromium and Firefox the browser puts the panel straight after its button in the tab order, wherever the panel sits in the markup; WebKit was not measured, because its Tab key skips links and buttons by default. A panel is not modal: the page behind stays usable, and a click outside closes it. For a panel that holds a form, make it a dialog element with aria-labelledby naming its heading, so a screen reader announces a named dialog and autofocus on a field works. Do not open it on hover, and keep a menu of links in a dropdown.

guarded: anchor positioning, position-try (fallback: the panel is centered by the user agent)
